questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Tola arrived at the library before it opened, yet six students were already waiting. What can be inferred from the sentence?
options: Several students were eager to use the library
The library opened late every day
The six students arrived after Tola
questions.explanation: Their presence before opening most directly suggests that several students were eager to use the library.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: A paragraph explains that trees cool cities, reduce flooding and improve air quality. Which title best captures its main idea?
questions.explanation: All three details describe benefits that trees provide in urban areas, so the broad title covers the whole paragraph.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In the statement 'After the debate, the principal poured oil on troubled waters,' the principal did what?
questions.explanation: To pour oil on troubled waters is to calm a disagreement or reduce tension between people.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined idea: The accountant was meticulous in checking the figures.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means extremely careful and attentive to small details.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Clean water was SCARCE after the drought.
questions.explanation: Scarce means limited or difficult to find; abundant means available in large quantities.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: When Kemi 'spilled the beans', she did what?
questions.explanation: To spill the beans is an idiom meaning to reveal information that was meant to remain secret.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the word most closely associated with a surgeon's work.
questions.explanation: A scalpel is a small, sharp instrument used by surgeons during operations.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Hardly had the match begun ___ the rain started.
questions.explanation: The standard construction is 'hardly had ... when' to show that one event followed another immediately.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: Each of the players ___ a locker.
questions.explanation: The subject 'each' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: We congratulated Ada ___ winning the scholarship.
questions.explanation: The verb 'congratulate' takes the preposition 'on' before an achievement.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: Let us begin the meeting, ___?
questions.explanation: Suggestions beginning with 'let us' normally take the question tag 'shall we?'.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The committee put off the inspection,' what does 'put off' mean?
questions.explanation: In this context, the phrasal verb 'put off' means delayed or postponed to a later time.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that means Musa can enter only if he presents his card.
options: Musa may enter unless he presents his card.
Unless Musa presents his card, he cannot enter.
Musa cannot enter because he presented his card.
Although Musa presents his card, he cannot enter.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the sentence makes presenting the card a condition for entry.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the expression: The board will ___ a decision tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The standard English collocation is 'make a decision'.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the teachers nor the principal ___ available.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject; singular 'principal' takes 'was'.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which word contains the same consonant sound represented by 'th' in 'thin'?
questions.explanation: 'Thin' and 'thought' begin with the voiceless dental fricative /θ/; the other options use voiced /ð/.
